approachQuestion.prompt: Return the index path to the first negative integer in depth-first left-to-right order, or NONE if none exists. Each path component is a zero-based child index. A negative root integer has path []. Examples: [4,[2,-7],-1] returns [1,1]; [[],3] returns NONE; -2 returns [].
constraints: A value is either a signed 32-bit integer or an ordered list of values; lists may be empty.
The input is finite, acyclic, and has no shared subobjects. There are n total integer and list objects, including the root, with 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000; maximum nesting depth is h ≤ 1000.
Do not modify the input. Indexing a list, reading a tag, and integer comparisons take constant time.
The returned path is a fresh array, distinct from NONE.

options.text: Traverse children in order, keeping one mutable path buffer. Push an index before descending and pop it after an unsuccessful child; copy the path once at the first negative leaf and return that witness through all callers.
options.feedback: The buffer tracks the current location and the first witness is preserved all the way to the root.

options.text: Use the same ordered search but copy the entire path prefix before every child call, returning the first witness.
options.feedback: The result is correct, but repeated prefix copies are avoidable with one shared path buffer.

options.text: Search all children and always replace the saved witness with the newest negative leaf path.
options.feedback: For [-1,-2], the required answer is [0], not [1].

options.text: Call each child search but ignore its returned witness, returning NONE when the current object is a list.
options.feedback: For [[-1]], the valid witness [0,0] is lost during unwinding.

feedback.reason: Push a child index before descent and pop it on an unsuccessful return.
details: Keep a shared mutable index path. At a list, try children in index order by pushing the index, calling the helper, and popping if no witness was found. At the first negative integer, copy the current path into the result. Propagate that result immediately through the callers.

Push a child index before descent and pop it on an unsuccessful return. Copy only the first found path before shared backtracking changes it. Left-to-right child order determines which negative witness is first.

Push an index before descending and pop it after an unsuccessful child; copy the path once at the first negative leaf and return that witness through all callers.”: The buffer tracks the current location and the first witness is preserved all the way to the root.

“Search all children and always replace the saved witness with the newest negative leaf path.”: For [-1,-2], the required answer is [0], not [1].
“Call each child search but ignore its returned witness, returning NONE when the current object is a list.”: For [[-1]], the valid witness [0,0] is lost during unwinding.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze method-1 as described in the revealed method. Let n and h have the meanings in Q1. Use child indices and references without copying lists. Count active call frames; exclude input and returned output. There is no tail-call elimination. No hashing is used. Path push/pop is amortized constant time; copying a path of length d takes time and output storage proportional to d. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair among the options.

feedback.reason: A full unsuccessful search is linear; frames and the working path follow depth.
details: A no-negative input visits every object. The path buffer and active frames each follow depth; the single result copy adds at most depth work.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Nested calls remain active along a path; their storage must be counted.
“O(n²) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: Each object is processed once without rescanning or copying its descendants.
“O(h + 1) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: A shallow but wide input can still require inspecting every object.
